CS-BOOTCAMP-PROJECT-PROPOSAL / Summary / Bitcrushers

Predictive Mapping of Sargassum Proliferation through Satellite Imagery and Oceanographic Data

LITUS is a proposed web-based decision-support tool that helps Boracay stakeholders monitor Sargassum sightings and prepare for possible shoreline accumulation. It brings together available satellite observations, wind and ocean-current information where accessible, and reports from people on the ground in one map-based dashboard. The goal is practical: help local authorities and beach-cleaning teams decide which areas to inspect first, when to prepare staff and equipment, and how to coordinate a response. LITUS will not claim to predict every event accurately. During the bootcamp, the team will build a feasible prototype with a limited Boracay study area, public data, a basic risk display, and field-reporting features.

Explore the proposal View the pilot plan
01 / Problem Background

When the Coast Changes, Preparation Matters.

Sargassum is a floating brown seaweed that can provide a habitat for marine life. However, when large amounts accumulate and decompose along beaches, they may cause unpleasant odors, affect beach use, and increase the workload of coastal cleaning teams. These effects matter in Boracay, where beach conditions are important to tourism, local livelihoods, and environmental management. The project addresses a practical coastal-management need: making useful information easier to access before teams decide where to inspect or clean.

Shoreline impacts

Decomposing seaweed may cause unpleasant odors and affect beach use.

Limited preparation time

Late reports can leave teams less time to organize workers, equipment, and transport.

Scattered information

Observations, satellite imagery, and ocean-condition data may be spread across different sources.

Community and tourism

Coastal conditions matter to visitors, local livelihoods, and environmental management.

02 / Proposed Solution

Proposed Solution

LITUS will provide a map-based dashboard showing available satellite observations, recent field or community reports, and an indication of areas that may need inspection. Where suitable wind and ocean-current data are available, the prototype may show an exploratory drift direction or accumulation-risk category. Users will be able to view the latest observation date, submit shoreline reports, compare locations, and receive demonstration alerts when selected thresholds are reached. The first version will prioritize a working, testable dashboard over a complex forecasting model.

The proposed first version would include:

  • 01

    A map showing recent observations and reported Sargassum sightings.

  • 02

    A simple classification of observed areas, such as “no clear detection”, “possible presence”, or “reported shoreline accumulation”.

  • 03

    A short-term drift or risk estimate when the required oceanographic data are available.

  • 04

    A field report form for location, date, photo, and approximate accumulation level.

  • 05

    A dashboard for comparing locations and reviewing historical reports.

  • 06

    Alerts based on defined thresholds, with the date of the latest data and an uncertainty notice.

To keep the project feasible, the minimum viable prototype will focus on one limited area of Boracay, a map interface, sample or publicly available observations, a field report form, and simple risk categories or threshold-based alerts. A sophisticated machine-learning model and reliable day-by-day beaching forecasts are outside the initial scope unless the team obtains suitable local training data, technical support, and validation. This limited approach allows the team to demonstrate the core idea and test whether users find it helpful.

03 / Objectives

Objectives

General objective

To develop and test a feasible prototype that organizes available satellite, oceanographic, and field report information to help Boracay stakeholders monitor possible Sargassum accumulation and plan inspections or cleanup responses.

  • 01

    Build a simple map dashboard for viewing available Sargassum observations and field reports in a limited Boracay pilot area.

  • 02

    Display available wind and ocean-current information and, if the data support it, demonstrate a basic drift or accumulation risk estimate.

  • 03

    Create a field report form for recording a location, date, photograph, and approximate accumulation level.

  • 04

    Use clear categories and timestamps to help users identify areas that may need closer inspection.

  • 05

    Show data limitations and uncertainty so users understand that alerts indicate a possible risk, not a guaranteed event.

  • 06

    Collect feedback from potential users or knowledgeable stakeholders, if access can be arranged, and use it to assess clarity, feasibility, and usefulness.

05 / Value Proposition

Value Proposition

LITUS aims to turn separate environmental observations into information that is easier to use for local decisions. Its intended practical value will be to help users answer three questions:

01

Where should teams inspect first?

02

When should they prepare?

03

Which locations may need closer monitoring?

The project's proposed innovation is its local focus and its combination of map-based observations, community or field reports, simple risk categories, and operational planning into one accessible prototype. Since satellite monitoring and Sargassum forecasting already exist, LITUS will be presented as a localized adaptation and workflow improvement, not as the first system of its kind. Its value and differences must be checked through user interviews and a review of existing services.

06 / Business Model

Business Model

The initial version could be developed as a civic-technology or research prototype. If testing shows that it is useful, sustainability could come from one or more of the following approaches:

01

Public sector partnership: An LGU or environmental office that can support hosting, maintenance, or further development.

02

Research partnership: A university or marine science group that can contribute validation data, technical guidance, or research funding.

03

Service agreement: A tourism or coastalmanagement organization that can pay for tailored dashboards, reports, or training.

04

Grant support: Environmental, climate resilience, or innovation grants that can help continued development.

Note: LITUS will initially be developed and tested as a prototype. Future funding or partnerships are needed to operate it as a live service.

07 / Market Analysis

Market Analysis

The initial target users are organizations and teams involved in coastal monitoring, beach maintenance, marine conservation, and tourism operations in Boracay. The project is intentionally limited to one pilot location to make development and testing realistic during the bootcamp. If testing shows that the approach is useful and can be maintained, it could later be adapted to other Philippine coastal areas after checking local conditions, data availability, and user needs.

01

Current alternatives may include manual shoreline inspections, reports shared through messaging applications, general satellite-data viewers, and Sargassum monitoring or forecasting platforms developed for other regions. These approaches may already meet some needs. LITUS will test whether a simple localized dashboard that brings observations and field reports together can make information easier to interpret and support planning. This comparison is important before claiming that the project is unique or that demand is already established.

02

Before claiming market demand, the team will interview potential users and review existing services. Validation questions include: “How are Sargassum events currently monitored?” “How much notice is useful?” “Which data are trusted?” “What decisions would a forecast change?” “Who would maintain reports and verify observations?” “What level of prediction uncertainty is acceptable?”

08 / Operations Plan

Operations Plan

Phase 1

Confirm the Need

Review evidence and consult local beach cleaners, environmental staff, tourism partners, or marine researchers to pinpoint key decision-making needs.

Phase 2

Confirm Usable Data

Pick a focused Boracay pilot site and confirm access to reliable public satellite, wind, ocean current, and ground observation data.

Phase 3

Build the Minimum Viable Prototype

Develop a web map featuring observation logs, filters, reporting forms, and risk alerts, adding drift forecasting if data permits.

Phase 4

Check the Results

Validate displayed data against local shoreline reports, transparently noting any missing entries, false positives, or uncertainties.

Phase 5

Test with Users

Have stakeholders perform basic tasks, like checking recent reports or spotting priority inspection zones, to evaluate usability and clarity.

Phase 6

Maintenance and Improvement

Designate owners for data moderation, maintenance, and support, scaling the project only after evaluating pilot outcomes.

Required resources

  1. Web developer/technical team
  2. Coastal data and report sources
  3. Internet access and hosting
  4. Personnel for review and validation
  5. Clear procedures for inaccurate reports and state privacy

Financial Requirement

The following is a preliminary planning estimate for a student-built prototype and should not be considered as a confirmed project budget. It assumes that team members use their own computers, open-source software, and publicly accessible data where available. The estimated costs will be reviewed after the team confirms the project scope, data requirements, travel needs, and validation plan.

Preliminary Estimated Budget for Prototype Development:

Expense Estimated Cost (PHP) Purpose
Domain and basic hosting ₱1,500–₱4,000 Publish the prototype and provide access for testing.
Connectivity and data handling ₱1,000–₱2,500 Internet, data transfer, and storage needs.
Field validation / local transport ₱3,000–₱8,000 Possible travel and coordination for shoreline observations.
Printing and user testing materials ₱500–₱1,500 Forms, documentation, and demonstration materials.
Contingency ₱1,000–₱3,000 Unexpected small expenses.
Indicative total ₱7,000–₱19,000 Prototype-stage estimate only

The estimate excludes salaries, paid satellite imagery, specialized oceanographic modeling services, laboratory work, and large-scale deployment. If travel and paid services are not required, costs may be lower. If reliable field validation or specialized technical support is needed, costs may be higher. The team should obtain actual quotations before presenting a final funding request.

10 / Scope, Risks, and Limitations

Scope, Risks, and Limitations

Project Boundaries & Pilot Area Constraints

Geographic focus

The initial system deployment and validation scope is strictly constrained to the coastal waters of Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan, serving as the primary pilot zone due to historical vulnerability to algal and Sargassum accumulation.

Administrative scope

The prototype is built to support up to 5 local government units (LGUs) or municipal environmental management offices concurrently during its initial phase.

Risks and Limitations

Cloud cover, sun glint, shallow water, turbidity, and satellite resolution can affect Sargassum detection.

Forecasts can be wrong; maps must show observation dates, confidence or uncertainty, and data gaps.

Sargassum sightings submitted by users may be incomplete or incorrectly identified and need verification procedures.

Local field observations and expert input may be difficult to obtain during a student project.

The tool should support, not replace, decisions made by local environmental authorities and marine specialists.
